en:
The concert at the Dome didn't work out, but it looked like
you at least had some good news back there.
Something new crop up?

Yes. The day after tomorrow, T-Set and I are putting on a
new concert at the Japan Dome!
Huh? The Japan Dome?

I'm not too clear on the details, but our president and the
head of Osaka Talent planned it together.
We didn't know about it until now.
Really, I couldn't be happier.
You said you were watching TV with him, right?
Did you come all the way from Fukuoka to give me that message?
Uh, no, actually...

It's just like him to get someone else to do the hard work.
He could have just called.
Don't you think?
Umm...?

Haruka-chan, Kiryu-san is actually here in Kamurocho right
now.

It sounds like there was some trouble with his old job, so
he came on a short business trip.
He's out right now, but he's staying close by.
Some place called New Serena.

Haruka-chan, I know I just passed on that message from
Kiryu-san.

But do you really have your heart set on performing in that
concert?
Huh? Why do you ask?
I just have a feeling that something bad might happen...
Hm? Like what?

I'm not sure. You said this concert came together out of the
blue, right?
That makes it even more suspicious.

The Japan Dome isn't the kind of place you can just decide
to put on a show.
Doesn't that seem off to you?
Well, I guess so, but...
Look, Kiryu-san is having a rough time now.

A close friend of his got in an accident and is in real bad
shape.
Really? Who?
I don't really know myself, but he's taking it pretty hard.

I think he might be on the verge of doing something
reckless.

He may be strong, but when you lose someone close, even the
stoutest heart can falter.
If you could just go see him...
I bet it'd do him more good than anything else ever could.

What do you say? You're still young. You don't need to be in
a rush to have this concert.

There'll always be another chance to get on stage at the
Dome when you're ready.

Do you think you could be there for Kiryu-san in his hour of
need?
I'm sorry... I can't do that right now.

Uncle Kaz is a kind person, so I can understand that he's
really upset about his friend.
But I get the feeling that if I go to see him...
We'll both lose something even more important.
Something more important?
Yes. It's hard to explain...

I guess I just feel like I could lose something I've always
had faith in.
I believe in Uncle Kaz.

That's why I'll keep walking the path that he's sacrificed
so much to send me down.
Thank you. I appreciate you giving me his message.

I should get going now. I still have lots of lessons to get
through.
Haruka-chan. Do you have time for one more question?

You never asked how Kiryu-san and I knew each other. You
didn't even ask my name.
How did you know you could trust me?

Well, I can see you're the sort of person Uncle Kaz would be
friends with.

Yep. Over the years, I've learned the people he takes a
liking to have certain things in common.
Is that right...?

I could tell you weren't a bad guy, at least. I guess that
doesn't really answer your question, though.
No, that's all right. All good.
Well then, I'd better go.
Damn it. What am I doing?
Haruka can now travel to Sotenbori by taxi.
(I don't need to visit the lesson studio.)

(If I go back to training now, I won't have any free time
until after the show.)

(This is my last chance to wander around town. Should I go
back to training?)

(Should I really go back to training? Is there anything I
should do first?)
(I can afford to walk around a little bit more.)
(Okay, time to focus!)

So if some creep were planning to kill Haruka-chan with a
rifle...
The only clear shot's from the outfield stands, is that what you're saying?

Right. Going off these plans, it looks like the stage'll be
just over home plate.
That narrows it down even more.

The only viable spot would be here, next to the batter's eye
screen.

How're ya so sure? Looks like there's plenty of other
options to me.

The other spots either have too many people around or make
it hard to get a clear shot.
When you take into account the scaffolding, lighting, and camera positions...
This is the only spot you get a direct bead on home plate.
You talk like you've done this before.

Baseball's one thing, but it's not like you've ever been
shot at before, right?
How can you be sure they'll choose that place?
Just trust me! It has to be here.
I'm no sniper, but in the world of pro baseball...
The home team often posts spies there.
Spies?
They're stealing signs.

You can see the opposing catcher's hand signals through
binoculars from there.
Then you radio them over to the bench.

So pro baseball batters know what balls're getting pitched
to them?
Not all of them, no.

At crucial points in the game, teams often try to intercept
the hand signals.

Hold on. You were accused of stealing signals in that
scandal fifteen years ago.
Was that really the case?

No. Normally, when the game is on the line like that, the
Wyverns would be doing everything they could to win.

They'd have a spy here in the center field stands to
intercept the signals.

Then it'd be the third base coach's job to pass the info
on to me.
But on that day, nobody was in the center field stands.
So you didn't know what was coming?
Right. That's why I was able to hit that home run.

If I'd been told what the sign was, I doubt I ever could
hit that fastball.
No kidding... Funny how life works out sometimes, huh?
You hit a home run because you didn't know what was coming.

Yet you were still accused of stealing signs and got thrown
out of the league.
Why didn't you say so fifteen years ago?
You could have proved you were innocent.
Sure... But I could've never gone through with it.
I didn't want to ruin the dreams of the fans.

Nobody knows stuff like that's going on in the sport they
love so much.
They wouldn't want to know.

They just want the thrill of watching us play, to live out
the dreams they never fulfilled.
I hit one home run over the course of my entire career.
But for some people, that was all they ever needed to see.
The same goes for this concert.

The people watching Haruka-chan up on that stage are gonna
be inspired to chase their own dreams.
People need to see others following their dreams like that.
It makes it a lot less scary to start chasing your own.

Dreams are passed on from one person to another, changing
each time.

Like how Sawada inspired me and I went on to inspire
Dojima-kun.

Dojima-kun put his life on the line to protect his dream,
and now it's my turn to help keep it alive.

Yeah, I gotta see my brother's dreams through to the end,
too.
Well said.
Like I said, you can't get in this way.
It's not like at a baseball game.

What about this gate, then? You could slip in to the
outfield seats through here.
Nice seein' you again, Kiryu-san.

This is a layout of the Japan Dome. We're drawing up a
sketch of tomorrow's concert.
Tomorrow?
You told Haruka-chan to never give up, didn't you?

She said so when I went to pick up these plans. She said she
got your message.
You could've told us sooner, you know? Right, Saejima-san?
Heh... Yeah.
Let's review what we know about the concert gates, shall we?
Who's this guy?
The concert at the Dome's in danger?
Yeah, that's the main thing I wanted to talk to you about.

Haruka-chan is about to perform her major debut concert at
the Japan Dome.
But we think there's some serious trouble brewing.
I thought that concert got canceled.

No, Katsuya actually just pulled some strings to change the
date from today to tomorrow.

And now Haruka-chan'll be performing with her rivals from
Osaka Talent.
Some kind of supergroup with T-Set.

T-Set? Weren't they the group set to do the concert in
Haruka's place?

That's right. I'm pretty sure they're practicing their big
debut song as we speak.
So what's this threat to the concert all about?

I think Katsuya realized Kurosawa was targeting
Haruka-chan's original concert.
So he canceled it to prevent anything from happening.
Why would Kurosawa target Haruka?
My guess is it's a backup plan.

If he fails to kill Kiryu-san, then threatening
Haruka-chan would be the next best thing.
Now that ya mention it, Kurosawa did say somethin'.
He said Kiryu better watch out for Haruka.

But holding a concert at the Dome was something Park-san and
Katsuya had wanted for so long.

So I think he changed the day, hoping that would dodge the
threat to Haruka-chan...
What's more, she'd still have the chance to perform.
It didn't go according to plan, though.

I imagine Katsuya wanted to end things with Kurosawa last
night.

But Kurosawa got away. And even if we wanted to cancel the
concert, Katsuya is in no condition to make the necessary
calls.
Real "rock and a hard place" situation we're in.
So what's your plan now?

We have to stop Kurosawa's men from getting into the concert
tomorrow.

Failing that, our only option is to either postpone the
concert or cancel it.
Cancel it, huh?
I guess that's unavoidable.

It's a concert at the Japan Dome. You're talking tens of
thousands of people going in and out.

Even if you stopped Kurosawa from getting in, there's no way
you'd be able to weed out all his men.
Yeah, it's a tough call.

Up until today, I was all for helping Haruka-chan get her
chance in the spotlight.
But with Kurosawa mucking things up, we don't have a choice.
Kiryu-san...!?
How are you still walking?
You can't cancel the concert, no matter what.
Did you hear all of that?
Yeah, I got the gist.

Then, surely you understand how risky it is to go ahead
with it.
I do.
Then, why?

Because even if Haruka heard what was going on, she'd still
choose to be on that stage.

You knew that before you came here to talk with us, didn't
you?

And you also know I'm probably the only one who could
convince her to pull out.

You got me there. Haruka-chan would go on with the concert
even if she knew the risk.
But if you told her to drop it, Kiryu-san, she'd listen.

Are you willing to put her up on that stage knowing that
her life is at stake?
Hey, Kiryu.

So you already know that Kurosawa, chairman of the Omi
Alliance, is behind all this?
Yeah. Saejima filled me in before you got here.
Kurosawa said he did it all to get rid of Kiryu and the rest of the Tojo's top brass...
As well as Watase and Katsuya on his own side.

Right. This all came about after he learned he was going to
die.

Kurosawa anticipated the Tojo Clan going to Fukuoka,
Sapporo, and Nagoya, and arranged to have their top men killed.
But he never planned for what happened in Osaka.
What happened in Osaka?
This letter.

Everything revolved around a letter Majima-san sent to his
former wife, Park-san.

That sparked some trouble between Katsuya's Ousaka
Enterprises and Dyna Chair, where Haruka-chan is signed.
Majima's former wife? Did you know about that, Saejima?

That's right... Thought I'd heard the names Katsuya and Park
before.
I heard Majima talk about 'em once after I got out.

No doubt they wanted to keep it quiet, given the positions
they ended up in.
I guess not many people knew Majima-san was once married.
So how about this letter? Why's it so important?

Majima-san sent it to his former wife, the president of Dyna
Chair⑬the agency where Haruka-chan is signed.
Her name was Mirei Park.

Funny thing is, the postmark shows it was sent after
Majima-san was supposedly killed in Sapporo.
It was postmarked after his death?

Right. Not only that, but the letter indicated Majima-san's
whereabouts.

When the people at Ousaka Enterprises learned this, they
figured Majima-san was still alive.

They thought getting a hold of the letter would help pin
down his location.

Which sadly led to Park-san's death and the letter being
passed down to Haruka-chan.
Next thing you know, she's Ousaka Enterprises' next target.
Hold on a sec. You're telling me Majima is still alive?
No, I don't think so, unfortunately.

If he were alive, he would have come after Kurosawa last
night.
But he didn't show.

It's likely he was already dead by the time Park-san
received the letter.
Then how did Majima get the letter over to this Park woman?

Katsuya. Majima-san must have left the letter with Katsuya
from the beginning.
What!? I don't get it.
Something was bugging me, though.

How on earth would the people at Ousaka Enterprises know
about the letter? It just didn't add up.
